data.reasoning_text:

1. `document-title` - no title (serious)
2. `html-has-lang` - no lang attribute (serious)

But the index.html clearly has `<html lang="en">` and `<title>Contact Support — Acme</title>`.

The initial state works fine with the `<html lang>` and `<title>` present, but they're failing in the error and success states even though we're using the same `page.setContent()` call. I think the real problem is that `app.js` isn't loading because the relative path doesn't resolve when using `setContent()` without a proper base URL. Since the script fails to load, the form submission handler never attaches, so clicking the button triggers a normal form submission that navigates away from the page—which would explain why the initial state passes but the error state fails, since the page content disappears after navigation.

To fix this properly, I should either serve the files through a local HTTP server or inline the JavaScript directly into the test so it actually runs. I'll set up a simple Node HTTP server to serve the files, run the axe accessibility tests against localhost, and then shut it down when done.
